2. The legal fixed Petz square and its actual compatibility witness.

Put Gamma(X)=sigma^{1/2}Xsigma^{1/2}, G=Gamma^{1/2},
 T=G^{-1}Phi G, Phi^sharp=Gamma Phi^* Gamma^{-1}, S=Phi^sharp Phi.
Gamma and its inverse are CP congruences, so Phi^sharp is CP. Its adjoint
Gamma^{-1}Phi Gamma fixes I because Phi(sigma)=sigma; therefore Phi^sharp
is TP. Also Phi^sharp(sigma)=Gamma Phi^*(I)=sigma.

The actual full-domain CPTP broadcaster
 mathcal B_S=(Phi^sharp tensor Phi^sharp) mathcal B
has BOTH marginals S on every matrix input. The other postprocessing is TP,
so taking either output marginal commutes with that postprocessing. Thus S
is genuinely self-compatible, sigma stationary, and state independent.

Its physical weighted implementation is
 T_S=G^{-1}S G=T^dagger T.
This is a positive HS-self-adjoint operator. It is similar to the CPTP S,
whose spectrum has modulus <=1: its adjoint is UCP and hence contracts the
operator norm. Consequently 0<=T^dagger T<=I, and T is an HS contraction.
Equivalently S^* is KMS-self-adjoint at sigma, so all premises of the old
weighted C4 theorem hold for S even though they need not hold for Phi.
No trace residual for S is inferred or needed.

It therefore tensors with id_HS(R) for EVERY finite reference.
